claims.text: The RHEA design space contains a vast number of possible compositions that requires efficient exploration tools.
Machine-learning-based multi-objective optimization can be applied to RHEA composition space.
Machine-learning-based multi-objective optimization will yield new near-equiatomic RHEA formulations.
The resulting formulations will have improved strength, ductility, and density relative to trial-and-error or single-objective design.
A near-equiatomic RHEA composition library with mechanical-property data from experiments and databases is available for model training.
The proposed data-driven optimization jointly considers specific strength, ductility, and density.
Comparable synthesis and processing conditions allow candidate RHEAs to be assessed through subsequent mechanical testing.
The candidate RHEAs will have predominantly BCC-based microstructures.
Predominantly BCC-based microstructures affect conventional slip and twinning mechanisms in RHEAs.
Multi-objective machine-learning models can correlate compositional variation with measured mechanical responses.
Multi-objective optimization encourages exploration of composition-space regions that balance strengthening, ductility, and low density.
ML-designed RHEAs will exhibit yield strength greater than 1800 MPa.
ML-designed RHEAs will exhibit ductility above 10%.
ML-designed RHEAs will have reduced density relative to RHEAs developed by trial-and-error methods.
Incremental alloy-design and CALPHAD-based approaches often underexplore the design space and require extensive experimental iteration.
CALPHAD is an established tool in advanced HEA design.
Insufficient high-fidelity training data may cause ML predictions to underperform.
Highly nonlinear and underrepresented elemental interactions may cause ML predictions to underperform.
Quantitative improvements in yield strength and ductility are uncertain because of limited RHEA datasets and model-generalization limitations.
